# London Leaking Ceiling: Immediate Tenant Action Plan

You have a strong repair issue, especially with **water damage** and a **3-week delay** after repeated written requests. The goal is to create a clear paper trail, set a firm deadline, and escalate if the landlord still does nothing.

## Practical Repair Escalation Plan

| Step | What to do | Timing | Goal |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Send one final written notice by email and text | Today | Give a clear deadline and record the issue |
| 2 | Attach photos, dates, and a brief damage list | Today | Prove the leak and the impact on your belongings |
| 3 | Request a repair date and contractor visit | Today | Force a specific response, not vague promises |
| 4 | If no reply, contact the landlord’s agent or managing agent | After deadline passes | Escalate to the next responsible party |
| 5 | Report the hazard to the local council environmental health / housing team | If still ignored | Trigger an official inspection or enforcement |
| 6 | Protect belongings and keep receipts for any losses | Ongoing | Support a future compensation claim |
| 7 | Do not withhold rent without legal advice | Ongoing | Avoid creating a rent arrears problem |

## Document Checklist for the Leaking Ceiling

- Emails dated **2026-02-02**, **2026-02-09**, and **2026-02-16**
- Photos or short videos of:
  - the leak
  - ceiling staining or sagging
  - wet patches
  - damaged furniture
- A simple timeline of events, including when the leak started
- Names of anyone you spoke to by phone, with dates and times
- Copies of any text messages or WhatsApp messages
- A list of damaged items and estimated replacement cost
- Receipts for any temporary protective measures or cleaning
- Your tenancy agreement and landlord/agent contact details
- A copy of the final repair request you send now
- Any response from the landlord, even if it is brief or dismissive

## Polite but Firm Repair Message

Subject: Urgent repair request: leaking ceiling and water damage

Hello [Landlord/Agent Name],

I am writing again about the leaking ceiling in my flat. I first reported this on **2026-02-02**, followed by further emails on **2026-02-09** and **2026-02-16**, but the issue still has not been fixed.

The leak is now causing **water damage to furniture**, and the condition of the flat is worsening. This needs to be treated as an urgent repair.

Please confirm:
- when a contractor will inspect the leak
- the date the repair will be completed
- what temporary steps will be taken to prevent further damage

I would appreciate a written response within **48 hours** and a repair timeline as soon as possible. If I do not hear back, I will have to consider escalating the matter through the relevant housing and environmental health channels.

Please treat this as urgent.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Your address]
[Your phone number]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Send email] mailto:?subject=Urgent%20repair%20request%3A%20leaking%20ceiling%20and%20water%20damage
Action: [Button: Find council] https://www.gov.uk/find-local-council
Action: [Button: Tenant rights] https://www.gov.uk/private-renting/repairs
Action: [Button: Shelter advice] https://england.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/repairs

## Useful References

- UK private renting repairs guidance: https://www.gov.uk/private-renting/repairs
- Find your local council: https://www.gov.uk/find-local-council
- Shelter repairs advice: https://england.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/repairs
